subject.title: [Bug]: Block streaming can drop paragraph separators across streamed updates

question: Should the shared block-streaming fix preserve paragraph separators in chunk text with smart coalescing, require explicit boundary metadata through the delivery pipeline, or reject the current candidates in favor of another design?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but two open candidate PRs implement the in-band separator approach and the issue also names explicit metadata as an alternative; automation should not choose the permanent streaming contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Consolidate an in-band separator fix
options.body: Review and land one current candidate, or consolidate them, if maintainers accept preserving paragraph separators on emitted chunks plus coalescer seam handling as the narrow shared fix.

options.title: Require boundary metadata
options.body: Ask for a replacement design that carries paragraph/newline/hard-split metadata through the pipeline if maintainers want text payloads to remain separator-normalized.

options.title: Pause the current candidates
options.body: Keep the issue open but close or pause both candidate PRs if neither approach matches the intended block-streaming contract.

recommendation.title: Consolidate an in-band separator fix
recommendation.body: Review and land one current candidate, or consolidate them, if maintainers accept preserving paragraph separators on emitted chunks plus coalescer seam handling as the narrow shared fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work spans embedded-agent helper documentation, auto-reply block helpers, streaming docs, and adjacent reply pipeline fixes, making this the best available routing signal for the boundary choice.
